Lighter rendering

Historical comparison of the original v23 scene and the three v24 detail levels, on the same machine with the same workload. Four cases on the generic 10 m boat with gradual halyard and speed changes.

These numbers measure scene CPU time with only the GPU backend stubbed. They are not browser FPS and do not measure GPU time. For your device, use View → Graphics and performance → Performance monitor. Pressures, physics accuracy and AUTO remain unchanged.

120 measured frames after 30 warmup frames per case. Physics evaluation time is excluded. Median, 95th percentile and per-phase timings are included in the JSON. Repeat the benchmark with scripts/profile-render.mjs; this does not replace visual WebGL testing on real devices.

What to tune

  1. Turning off shadows reduces shadow-map work.
  2. Essential reduces visual grids, decoration and update rates. Telltale stations and wind contacts are preserved.
  3. Rendering follows the display refresh rate. Dense wind streams, pressure colouring and additional force groups add work.

Unchanged rope buffers and colour palettes are reused. Geometry and animation updates are scheduled separately, hidden wake work is skipped and rendering pauses in hidden pages. Continuous main-thread pressure calculations and wind contact searches remain further optimisation areas; moving them to workers or accelerating them requires testing trim latency and consistency.
